react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms (RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and Mummichog m/z-directed activity) converge on a unified biological story centred on one-carbon amino-acid metabolism and connected methyl-group biology. The top cross-paradigm winner is the Glycine, Serine and Threonine metabolism superpathway (RaMP KEGG:map00260 rank-1, FDR 8.6e-17, 7 of 57 pathway metabolites hit; Mummichog MUMM:glycine_serine_alanine_and_threonine_metabolism rank-1, p=0.0035, 8 of 8 hit; MetaboAnalystR KEGG:hsa00260 rank-1, p=3.3e-7, 5 of 33 hit). Within this superpathway, glycine (C00037), L-serine (C00065), L-threonine (C00188) and L-cysteine (C00097) are the four driver compounds that co-occur across every tool. The second major axis is methionine metabolism (RaMP KEGG:map00270 FDR 1.1e-14, 6 of 51 hit; Mummichog MUMM:methionine_and_cysteine_metabolism rank-1, p=0.0092; MetaboAnalystR KEGG:hsa00270 rank-2, p=6e-4). S-adenosylmethionine (C00019, SAM) is the methyl-donor hub linking methionine catabolism to the folate cycle; adenosine (C00212) participates as the adenine moiety of SAM and as a purine node. Choline (C00114) bridges the one-carbon pool to glycerophospholipid metabolism (Mummichog MUMM:glycerophospholipid_metabolism rank-4, p=0.027) and appears as a shared hit in the folate superpathway (MetaboAnalystR KEGG:hsa00670 rank-0, p=8.4e-10). The cysteine node connects to the glutathione antioxidant pathway (RaMP REACT:R-HSA-71291 and Mummichog MUMM:glutathione_metabolism). Sucrose (C00089) and 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde (C04043) contributed to secondary hits in sialic-acid metabolism (Mummichog rank-2) and tyrosine metabolism (Mummichog rank-6) respectively, suggesting peripheral carbohydrate and monoamine-shunt perturbations. The convergent interpretation is that the treatment broadly dysregulates the interconnected serine/glycine/threonine/cysteine/methionine one-carbon network, with glycine and L-serine as the primary driver metabolites and SAM as the central methyl-group coordinator.

The mummichog m/z-network analysis confirms the same pathway with p-value 0.00126 and 8 of 8 input metabolites. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA places Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism at rank 2 with p-value 3.3e-07. A secondary cluster of enrichment centres on the methionine cycle, where S-adenosylmethionine drives the interlock with cysteine and serine metabolism. RaMP identifies KEGG:map00270 Methionine Metabolism at rank 9 with 6 metabolites hit, and MetaboAnalystR places Cysteine and methionine metabolism at rank 3 with p-value 0.0006. The two clusters are linked through the glycine N-methyltransferase reaction, which uses SAM to methylate glycine and connects the serine/threonine node to the one-carbon folate pool. Seven of the ten input metabolites cluster in these two pathways: glycine, L-serine, L-threonine, L-cysteine, choline, adenosine, and S-adenosylmethionine are all confirmed metabolites_hit members of Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism. The remaining three input compounds (3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde, sucrose, and L-2-amino-3-oxobutanoic acid) do not appear in the top pathway hit lists across any paradigm.
